test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 23 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Two cylindrical vessels have the same capacity and identical dimensions. If the radius of the first vessel is increased by 14 cm and the height of the second vessel is increased by 30 cm, the increase in capacity for both vessels is equal to Q cm³. If the actual height of each vessel is 24 cm, find the value of Q.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let radius = r, height = 24

Increase in volume:

1st: π[(r+14)² − r²] × 24 = π(28r + 196) × 24

2nd: πr²(24+30 − 24) = 30πr²

Equate ⇒ (28r + 196) × 24 = 30r²

⇒ r = 28

Q = 30πr² = 30π × 784 = 23520π

**∴ Answer = 23520π cm³**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height = 24 cm

Increase in radius = 14 cm

Increase in height = 30 cm

**Formula used:**

Volume of cylinder = πr²h

**Calculation:**

⇒ Original volume = πr² × 24

⇒ New volume (radius change) = π(r+14)² × 24

⇒ Increase = π[(r+14)² − r²] × 24

⇒ = π(28r + 196) × 24

⇒ New volume (height change) = πr² × 54

⇒ Increase = πr² × 30

⇒ Equate increases:

(28r + 196) × 24 = 30r²

⇒ 672r + 4704 = 30r²

⇒ r² − 22.4r − 156.8 = 0

⇒ r = 28 cm

⇒ Q = πr² × 30

⇒ = 30 × π × 28²

⇒ = 23520π cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 23520π cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cylinder Volume

V = πr²h

Change in Volume

Find difference between new and original volume

Key Idea

Equate both increases to find unknown radius
